“Education should only be in AI or center around AI and nothing else for everything to be in synchronisation.”

Pro argument

If the goal of education is synchronisation—between economy, governance, culture, science, and daily life—then centering education entirely around AI is a coherent and powerful proposition.

First, AI is a meta-discipline. Unlike traditional subjects that operate in silos (physics, economics, literature), AI absorbs and integrates them. Mathematics becomes algorithms, biology becomes bioinformatics, psychology becomes cognitive modeling, ethics becomes alignment research, and literature becomes language modeling. Instead of teaching many disconnected subjects, AI offers a single unifying framework.

Second, AI enforces standardisation without uniformity. When education revolves around AI systems, everyone learns through the same computational logic, data structures, and feedback loops—creating synchronization—while still allowing personalized learning paths. This resolves the classic conflict between equality and individuality in education.

Third, AI-centered education aligns directly with reality. Governance is algorithmic, markets are predictive, medicine is data-driven, warfare is autonomous, media is generated, and even relationships are mediated by recommendation systems. Teaching non-AI-first curricula prepares students for a world that no longer exists.

Fourth, AI collapses the lag between knowledge and application. Traditional education teaches theory first and relevance later. AI education is inherently applied—models must work, predictions must converge, outputs must be validated. This creates immediate feedback, reducing wasted years and misaligned skills.

Fifth, synchronisation is a survival strategy. In a world of rapid technological acceleration, desynchronized education creates social fragmentation—some groups living in the future, others trapped in obsolete paradigms. AI-only or AI-centered education keeps society temporally aligned.

Finally, AI becomes the common language of humanity. Just as literacy once unified civilizations, AI literacy can unify post-industrial societies. When everyone understands how intelligence is built, trained, biased, corrected, and governed, power becomes more transparent and collective decision-making becomes more rational.

In short, centering education exclusively around AI is not about narrowing knowledge—it is about compressing all knowledge into a single synchronised operating system for society.

video_title: But what is a neural network? | Deep learning chapter 1
text:
The calculation you mentioned refers to the total number of **weights** in a neural network, which represent the strength of connections between neurons in adjacent layers. In a network, every neuron in one layer is connected to every single neuron in the next layer.

Here is how the connections are broken down:

*   **Input to First Hidden Layer:** The input layer has 784 neurons (for a 28x28 pixel image), and the first hidden layer has 16 neurons. Since every input neuron connects to every hidden neuron, there are $784 \times 16$ individual weights (11:34).
*   **Between Hidden Layers:** There are two hidden layers, each with 16 neurons. The connections between these two layers require $16 \times 16$ weights.
*   **Last Hidden Layer to Output:** The final hidden layer has 16 neurons, and the output layer has 10 neurons (representing digits 0-9). This requires $16 \times 10$ weights.

**Why does this matter?**
Each connection has a specific **weight** that determines how much influence a neuron in one layer has on a neuron in the next. Along with **biases** (which determine the threshold for activation), these thousands of parameters form the "dials and knobs" of the network. During **training**, the computer adjusts these values so the network can accurately identify patterns, like handwritten digits (12:20-12:30).

One thing beginners often miss: not all indexes are equal. A composite index on (user_id, created_at) is very different from two separate indexes on each column. The query optimizer can only use one index per table scan in most cases, so a composite index lets you filter on user_id AND sort by created_at in a single B-tree traversal — massive difference on tables with millions of rows.

Also worth knowing: indexes slow down writes. Every INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE has to update the index too. So don't blindly index every column — profile your slow queries first, then index strategically.
